why: The founder's ruling of 28 October 2026, item 6: any sentence, Why? text or rationale that says or implies a cloud provider documents a behaviour carries the page's URL, the exact sentence quoted and the date read. The kit takes the shape of arvaken/mark's check (mark#914). A claim cites its entries by id, [source: id], in the README or in a comment or docstring, never in words a customer is shown. tests/test_provider_claims_name_their_source.py fails the build on a claim with no source.

fields.url: the page, https, on the provider's own host
fields.sentence: the sentence (or list, table row or entry) quoted whole, no ellipsis
fields.about: what the sentence is about, in the provider's own terms
fields.read: the day it was read, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC)

aws-s3-access-denied-example.sentence: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the GetObject operation: User: arn:aws:iam::777788889999:user/MaryMajor is not authorized to perform: s3:GetObject on resource: "arn:aws:s3:::amzn-s3-demo-bucket1/object-name" with an explicit deny in a resource control policy, with policy ARN: arn:aws:organizations::777788889999:policy/o-exampleorgid/resource_control_policy/p-examplepolicyid

google-storage-error-format.page: HTTP status and error codes for JSON | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation
google-storage-error-format.sentence: errors.reason: Example values include invalid, invalidParameter, and required. code: An HTTP status code value, without the textual description. Example values include: 400 (Bad Request), 401 (Unauthorized), and 404 (Not Found).
google-storage-error-format.about: the elements of the JSON API's error response, among them code and errors.reason, and no status

google-storage-403-forbidden.page: HTTP status and error codes for JSON | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation
google-storage-403-forbidden.sentence: forbidden: This error can occur for several reasons: According to access control policy, the current user does not have access to perform the requested action, and this can occur even if the resource being acted on doesn't exist; or the request is missing the overrideUnlockedRetention query parameter but is attempting to change an object's existing retention configuration in a way that requires the parameter; or the request is attempting to change a locked object's retention configuration in a way that requires the object to be unlocked.

google-storage-403-insufficient-permissi.page: HTTP status and error codes for JSON | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation
google-storage-403-insufficient-permissi.sentence: insufficientPermissions: According to access control policy, the current user does not have access to perform the requested action. This code applies even if the resource being acted on doesn't exist.

google-storage-401-auth-error.page: HTTP status and error codes for JSON | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation
google-storage-401-auth-error.sentence: authError: This error indicates a problem with the authorization provided in the request to Cloud Storage. The following are some situations where that will occur: The OAuth access token has expired and needs to be refreshed. This can be avoided by refreshing the access token early, but code can also catch this error, refresh the token and retry automatically. Multiple non-matching authorizations were provided; choose one mode only. The OAuth access token's bound project does not match the project associated with the provided developer key. The Authorization header was of an unrecognized format or uses an unsupported credential type.
google-storage-401-auth-error.about: the 401 Unauthorized reason authError, an expired access token among its situations

aws-lambda-vpc-permissions.page: Giving Lambda Event Functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC - AWS Lambda
aws-lambda-vpc-permissions.sentence: If you prefer to create your own IAM permissions policy, make sure to add all of the following permissions and allow them on all resources ("Resource": "*"): ec2:CreateNetworkInterface ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces ec2:DescribeSubnets ec2:DeleteNetworkInterface ec2:AssignPrivateIpAddresses ec2:UnassignPrivateIpAddresses
aws-lambda-vpc-permissions.about: the permissions a function's execution role needs for Lambda to attach the function to an Amazon VPC, and the resources to allow them on

aws-lambda-source-function-arn.page: Using source function ARN to control function access behavior - AWS Lambda
aws-lambda-source-function-arn.sentence: Lambda injects the source function ARN into the credentials context if the request is an AWS API request that comes from within your execution environment.
aws-lambda-source-function-arn.about: the source function ARN on AWS API requests from a function's execution environment

aws-lambda-source-function-arn-not-enis.page: Using source function ARN to control function access behavior - AWS Lambda
aws-lambda-source-function-arn-not-enis.sentence: Other AWS API calls that Lambda makes outside of your execution environment on your behalf using the same execution role don't contain the source function ARN. Examples of such API calls outside the execution environment include: Calls to AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to automatically encrypt and decrypt your environment variables. Calls to Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) to create elastic network interfaces (ENIs) for a VPC-enabled function. Calls to AWS services, such as Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS), to read from an event source that's set up as an event source mapping.
aws-lambda-source-function-arn-not-enis.about: the AWS API calls Lambda makes on a function's behalf that don't contain the source function ARN, among them Amazon EC2's to create ENIs for a VPC-enabled function

aws-iam-boundary-explicit-deny.page: Permissions boundaries for IAM entities - AWS Identity and Access Management
aws-iam-boundary-explicit-deny.sentence: Identity-based policies with boundaries – Identity-based policies are inline or managed policies that are attached to a user, group of users, or role. Identity-based policies grant permission to the entity, and permissions boundaries limit those permissions. The effective permissions are the intersection of both policy types. An explicit deny in either of these policies overrides the allow.
aws-iam-boundary-explicit-deny.about: evaluating identity-based policies with permissions boundaries: an explicit deny in either overrides the allow
